1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Peoples Farming, LLC operates a cold storage facility that uses a closed-loop ammonia refrigeration system servicing two buildings. Originally designed for tree fruit processing, the facility now supports hemp and licensed cannabis processing. Prior to Peoples Farming, LLC purchase of facility, modification managed via a formal Management of Change (MOC) process, the old mechanical rooms equipment was been disconnected and integrated into the main refrigeration system to optimize capacity and reduce costs.
This Risk Management Plan (RMP) summarizes our comprehensive approach to preventing and mitigating accidental ammonia releases. It includes succinct descriptions of our offsite consequence analyses, accident history, and our integrated prevention and emergency response programs. This document is submitted in accordance with EPA 40 CFR Part 68 and the California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) regulations.

2. INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE
This RMP has been developed to:
	Document Peoples Farming, LLCs compliance with federal and state

accidental release prevention regulations.
	Summarize the facilitys processes, particularly the ammonia refrigeration system.
	Describe our evaluation of potential risks from worst-case and alternative release scenarios.
	Provide a concise overview of our prevention, emergency response, and corrective action programs.
The purpose is to protect employees, nearby public receptors, and the environment by clearly outlining the safety protocols and management systems in place.

3. FACILITY AND PROCESS DESCRIPTION
	Process Overview:
The facility operates one closed-loop, single-stage ammonia refrigeration system with an inventory exceeding 10,000 lbs of anhydrous ammonia. This system serves two interconnected buildings used for hemp and licensed cannabis processing.
	Recent Modifications:
Through a documented MOC process, the older, separate refrigeration equipment has been decommissioned. The ammonia inventory has been fully transferred to the main system (completed in March 2020), with associated demo and new piping scheduled for completion within 90 days.
	Process Purpose:
Refrigeration is maintained strictly in a closed-loop system to ensure both operational efficiency and compliance with the Accident Prevention and Risk Management regulations.

4. REGULATORY COMPLIANCE SECTIONS
4.1 Registration Information
The facilitys registration detailsincluding address, emergency contacts, and owner/operator informationare maintained separately in Appendix A. (This section verifies that all details are current as per EPA and CalARP requirements.)
4.2 Offsite Consequence Analysis
Worst-Case Release Scenario:
	Substance: Ammonia (anhydrous)
	Scenario: A full rupture within the mechanical room, resulting in a rapid release.
	Key Metrics:
o	Quantity: (e.g., 16,500 lbs as modeled)
o	Estimated distance to endpoint:

Approximately 1.7 miles
o	Receptor count: Residential, school, and recreational areas impacted are summarized based on EPAs RMP*Comp modeling.
	Assumptions: Standard atmospheric conditions (e.g., wind speed ?1.5 m/s, stability class F) and conservative safety assumptions are used.
Alternative Release Scenario:
	Scenario: A minor pipe leak with a controlled release rate.
	Key Metrics:
o	Quantity: Approximately 360 lbs
o	Release Rate: 12 lbs/min over 30 minutes
o	Distance to endpoint: Approximately 0.1 miles
	Mitigation: Administrative controls, immediate isolation, and engineering safeguards are in place.
The detailed calculations and assumptions are documented in Appendix B.
4.3 Five-Year Accident History
Our historical review confirms that no reportable releases have occurred within the past five years. Routine internal audits and incident reviews (see Appendix C for details) validate this excellent safety record.

5. PREVENTION PROGRAM SUMMARY
The Prevention Program is designed to proactively manage risks associated with the ammonia refrigeration process and includes:
	Process Safety Information: Up-to-date safety data sheets, chemical hazard details, and equipment specifications are maintained.
	Process Hazard Analysis (PHA): Conducted using the What-If/Checklist methodology, with the most recent update on 01/27/2020. Key hazards (toxicity, overpressurization, corrosion, etc.) are identified.
	Operating Procedures: Written procedures cover all modes of operation including start-up, normal operations, emergency shutdown, and post-turnaround start-up.
	Training: All operators receive initial and refresher training at least every three years.
	Mechanical Integrity: Regular maintenance inspections and testing (aligned with IIAR and RAGAGEP guidelines) are performed.
	Management of Change (MOC): All modifications (e.g., the recent equipment consolidation) are managed through a

formal MOC process, with timely updates to process safety information.
	Pre-startup Reviews: New or modified processes undergo a pre-startup safety review to ensure compliance with safety standards.
	Compliance Audits: Audits are performed every three years with corrective actions documented and tracked.
	Incident Investigation: Each incident (or near miss) is thoroughly investigated with findings used to update the prevention program.
	Employee Participation: Employees are encouraged to participate and provide feedback; records of participation are maintained.
	Hot Work Permits & Contractor Management: Strict procedures for hot work and contractor safety are enforced.
A complete description of these components is provided in Appendix D.

6. EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM SUMMARY
Peoples Farming, LLC maintains a comprehensive Emergency Action Plan that includes:
	Emergency Notification: Procedures to alert on-site teams and local emergency responders immediately in case of an ammonia release.
	Evacuation Procedures: Clear evacuation routes and shelter-in-place instructions for employees and the public.
	Response Coordination: Regular drills and coordination with local fire departments and hazardous materials teams.
	Decontamination & Post-Incident Action: Steps for decontamination and environmental remediation are clearly outlined.
	Plan Reviews & Updates: The emergency plan is reviewed annually and updated promptly when changes occur (e.g., changes in emergency contacts).
Additional detailed procedures are available in Appendix E.

7. DOCUMENT CONTROL
This plan will be reviewed and updated at least every five years, or sooner if there is:
	A change in the regulated substance inventory,
	A material modification in process or equipment (as identified via the MOC process),
	A reportable incident that

affects the Accident History, or
	A change in emergency contact information.
A detailed log of all updates and revisions is maintained in Appendix F.

CONCLUSION
This streamlined Risk Management Plan consolidates critical safety information and regulatory compliance data in a manageable format while deferring extensive operational details to controlled appendices. This approach meets all federal and state requirements, improves clarity for regulators, and facilitates easier ongoing updates.
